page: The Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance within the Edsv6 family, powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor using x86_64 architecture. It allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Hardware features include an expansive 260 MB L3 cache, along with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix and vector operations. Memory allocation stands at 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU, complemented by 472 GB of NVMe SSD local storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-thread CPU performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded Gzip compression rate of 31.35 GB/sec. Text processing workloads also perform well, recording a Geekbench text processing score of 2554.0. Multi-threaded performance scales moderately, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 7392.44 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 4849.0. Conversely, heavily parallelized compute tasks and uncached memory operations show limitations, with stress-ng multi-core score placing in the lower performance quartile and uncached read memory bandwidth measured at 37.14 GB/sec.

With its substantial RAM density and local NVMe storage, the instance offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not require heavy multi-core processing. While unsuitable for dense parallel computing or large-scale machine learning generation (recording 4.5 tokens/sec on medium LLM text generation), its hardware profile fits in-memory caching, database operations, static web serving, and enterprise applications requiring high RAM per core.
